title: 21 June 2022, dollar/cad - news driver, sweep, shift, FVG, pool
looked_at: 08:30 New York high-impact core retail sales, 21 June 2022
a short-term high, then a run above it (buy-side taken)
the 15-minute and 5-minute charts side by side
decided: the shallow break was rejected; a more meaningful, energetic displacement was required
after the shift the FVG became the zone; equilibrium split the leg so the short needed an array below it
the stop had to sit at the far side of the imbalance used
postponed: taking the pre-news FVG ('a little bit more risky'); he waited for the news to create the setup
ruled_out: selling the first small break ('that's not enough')
htf_ltf: higher-timeframe context given first (where buy-side sits), execution read on the 5-minute, then dropped to the 4-minute to size the imbalance
expected_and_why: price to come back up and overlap the one-sided sell-side delivery, then deliver to the pool
outcome: stated: delivered to the fair value gap and then to the sell-side pool

title: Four opportunities per month - e-mini S&P income plan
looked_at: previous week's high/low and previous day's high/low
decided: one e-mini contract per trade, no pyramiding
static 4-point stop, 5.25-point / 21-tick target, one trade per session
trade only 09:30-11:30 or 13:30-15:30 New York local time
postponed: nothing discretionary is postponed - this is explicitly a mechanical plan
ruled_out: any FVG that does not permit a 4-point stop ('we do nothing we do not force higher risk')
htf_ltf: weekly range defines direction; 5-minute or lower for the shift; then 4/3/2/1-minute to select the FVG
expected_and_why: price sweeps the previous week's high/low, shifts structure, and reprices to a gap that fits the stop
outcome: not stated in the window read (the episode presents the template, not a live fill)

title: FX / Spooz review - dealing range and consequent encroachment
looked_at: the leg from that high down to that low as the dealing range
the four-hour chart because the daily was 'a whole lot of nasty price action'
decided: the run up stopped at a 15-minute bearish order block sitting at the consequent encroachment of the FVG
that half-of-the-range level is given as the reason for the reaction
postponed: the finer inefficiencies ('I'll talk a little bit more in detail ... when we get into the lower time frames')
ruled_out: calling the level random, Gann, Elliott, supply/demand or harmonic
htf_ltf: daily, then four-hour only when necessary, then watch each FVG get hit and rejected
expected_and_why: up-close candles resist in bearish order flow; down-close candles get eviscerated
outcome: stated: each run into the sell-side imbalance is rejected at its low, creating another sell-off

title: Bullish order block - validation then retrace entry
looked_at: an HTF support level (old low, or an old high traded back into)
the down-close candle at that level
decided: the down candle is only a suspected OB until a later candle trades through its high
once validated, the OB high is the retracement reference; risk below the OB low, raised to below 50% of the OB range
postponed: the entry may wait for the pullback if the retrace is missed
ruled_out: naming the candle an order block before validation
htf_ltf: HTF level for the zone, entry mechanics on the same chart
expected_and_why: after validation price pulls back to the OB high and can be bought there
outcome: not stated (teaching example, not a dated market)

title: Top-down routine - day of week, IPDA true day, killzone
looked_at: day of the week first (weekend analysis, Sunday open, Monday behaviour)
IPDA true day before any setup
decided: monthly/weekly/daily bias, then early-week (Mon-Wed) trades in that direction
the lower timeframe is whichever one actually shows the fair value gaps
postponed: late-week (Thu/Fri) templates are held back unless the early week fails
ruled_out: trading Monday-Wednesday when the expected influence did not appear
htf_ltf: 4H then 5M stated stack; the refiner chart is left to the trader
expected_and_why: weekly/daily templates repeat by weekday, so the day gates the setup
